title: IRL Black Friday was a horrifying spectacle. I miss it so much | Dave Schilling
summary: The days of coming to blows over a Furby before dawn are over. It was scary, but at least it was real Congratulations. You’re alive. And for that, I applaud you. You didn’t choke on a particularly large piece of pie or fall into a ditch on your post-Thanksgiving-meal walk. Thanksgiving is one of the more hazardous holidays on the American calendar, with all the binge eating, binge drinking and binge shopping. Continue reading...

title: Can Borussia Dortmund finally end their title wait? Three big questions for Bundesliga leaders
summary: Niko Kovac’s team lead the way and, with Bayern Munich wounded, have a golden chance to be German champions for the first time in 15 years Borussia Dortmund’s dreams have a habit of becoming nightmares, like when they somehow handed Bayern Munich the Bundesliga title on the final day of the 2022-23 season. Or when an 89th-minute Arjen Robben goal won the 2013 Champions League final for the same opponents. Whenever Dortmund suffer heartbreak, it usually involves Bayern. As things stand, however, Niko Kovac’s side hold a two-point lead over Bayern at the top of the Bundesliga. Both teams are unbeaten, but Dortmund may be the more stable of the two at the moment, especially with Harry Kane expected to miss several months through injury. Continue reading...

title: Bills, Eagles and Bears pull off last-gasp wins in trio of Thanksgiving thrillers
summary: Bass hits from 57 yards at the gun to lift Buffalo Elliott’s 59-yarder caps Eagles’ 21-point comeback Bears take NFC North lead on Odunze’s late catch After sharing top billing, Buffalo’s Josh Allen and Kansas City’s Patrick Mahomes proved no match for the elements in the latest showdown of two of the NFL’s best quarterbacks. With both offense’s failing to gain traction on a rainy, windy and cold Thursday night, the Bills improved their AFC-leading record to 10-1 by slogging through a 13-10 victory over the visiting Chiefs on Tyler Bass’s 57-yard field goal as time expired. Buffalo have won seven straight and matched their best start to a season since 1991. Continue reading...

title: Lights-out Luka and contagious chemistry: are these Lakers for real?
summary: It’s early days, but after a dramatic roster overhaul and an offseason of team-bonding Dončić is playing at an MVP level and LA are looking like contenders One of the components of Luka Dončić’s shock trade from the Dallas Mavericks to the Los Angeles Lakers that caused great consternation was that he was just entering his prime as an NBA superstar. The worry was that the move could end that prime before it really even began – unceremoniously uprooting the Slovenian wunderkind from a team custom built around his strengths, fresh off a run to the NBA finals, to one who didn’t really make sense at all. Sure, the bright lights of Hollywood would elevate Dončić’s profile and usher him into a new echelon of stardom. But with Oklahoma City starting their run of dominance and rising stars around the league waiting in the wings, some believed his hopes of title contention (or even a long-elusive MVP award) had vanished. But the start to this season raises the question: what if they were wrong? Dončić is neck-and-neck with Victor Wembanyama in the MVP race, and the Lakers have the best record in the NBA at 15-3, with the Spurs and 76ers just behind at 15-4. San Antonio and their gargantuan French superstar were title and MVP favorites by a wide margin entering this season. But Dončić and the Lakers are keeping pace by pretty much every margin. Friday night’s NBA Cup showdown will be a duel with ripple effects and stakes rarely seen in the regular season, let alone in November. The two best records. The two leading MVP candidates. A basketball fan couldn’t ask for much more. Continue reading...

title: Heavy rain, wind and flooding hit much of US on Thanksgiving
summary: Homes without power, travel disrupted and Macy’s Thanksgiving parade postponed for first time in New York Storms have flooded communities on the US east coast, knocking out power to nearly a million customers and prompting the first-ever postponement of Macy’s Thanksgiving Day parade in New York City. High winds and flooding hammered both coasts, disrupting holiday travel. More than 900,000 homes and businesses were without electricity on Thursday evening, with the majority in east coast states, according to the outage tracking website PowerOutage.us. More than 2,200 flights to or from US destinations were delayed and more than 400 were cancelled, according to the flight tracking service FlightAware. Continue reading...

title: King tides batter US coasts as storms threaten Thanksgiving celebrations
summary: Heavy rain, strong winds and coastal flooding creating hazardous conditions for millions travelling for holiday King tides and huge waves have been battering both coasts of the US during a turbulent Thanksgiving period, with severe weather threatening millions across the country. Along the California coast, king tides caused considerable damage. In Pacifica, south of San Francisco, large waves battered the coastline on Wednesday, destroying part of a pier and sending debris into the ocean. The National Weather Service issued coastal flood warnings covering parts of the Pacific coastline and shorelines around San Francisco Bay and San Pablo Bay. Several beachfront properties in Pacifica have already experienced flooding, while authorities in Marin County temporarily issued an evacuation warning for residents of beachfront homes at Stinson Beach.
